en: A fixed pulley changes the direction of your pull, allowing you to lift a heavy flag upward by pulling the rope downward.
The deep grooves on car tires increase friction with the road, preventing the wheels from slipping during rainy weather.
The Moon's gravitational pull on Earth's oceans causes the water to bulge, creating high and low tides every day.
Running an electric current through a coiled wire wrapped around an iron nail temporarily turns the nail into a magnet.
Closing a switch completes an electrical circuit, allowing electrons to flow through the wire and light up the connected bulb.
When white light enters a glass prism, it slows down and bends, separating into a rainbow of seven distinct colors.
Plucking a tight guitar string creates rapid vibrations that push surrounding air molecules, transmitting sound waves to your ears.
Heat travels from the hot soup to the metal spoon through conduction, making the handle warm to touch.
As a roller coaster car drops from a high hill, its stored potential energy transforms into fast kinetic energy.
Pushing a heavy box up a long wooden ramp requires less force than lifting the box straight up vertically.
Earth acts like a giant magnet, causing the magnetic needle inside a compass to always point toward the magnetic north.
Heating water at the bottom of a pot makes it less dense, causing it to rise while cooler water sinks.
